setting: A small rural settlement in a fantasy world where magic exists.
story: The protagonist is travelling through the settlement. No quest, conflict, solution or sequence of events is established.
assignment: Invent a short playable quest with an original purpose, dialogue and meaningful choices. Gather context through the tools and use only discovered references and supported capabilities. Publication does not start gameplay.
mechanics: WASD moves; Shift runs. E or a nearby click interacts. Select a carried item to use it on a nearby target or give it to a nearby character. NPC-to-protagonist transfers can be authored as consequences. Carrying a required weapon permits combat. Closed barriers and buildings block movement. Inspect discovered details and native schemas for supported interactions and prerequisites.

vocabulary.game_location: Inspect whether the protagonist is inside or has visited a location; count entries for new-event conditions.
vocabulary.game_encounter: Inspect remaining enemies in a group; count confirmed defeats. The protagonist defeats enemies through ordinary interaction, not an authoring action.
vocabulary.game_activate_group: Reveal undefeated enemies in an existing group when entering a quest stage.
vocabulary.game_reveal: Reveal an existing entity unless it was already defeated or collected.
vocabulary.game_open_gate: Open an existing gate as a quest consequence.
vocabulary.inventory_item: Inspect an item’s holder, quantity, contents and remaining uses; count protagonist acquisitions.
vocabulary.entity_state: Inspect a supported boolean state of an entity; count times that state became true.
vocabulary.give_item: Transfer an available item between its current holder and a nearby character. One endpoint must be the protagonist.
vocabulary.use_item: Use a carried item on a nearby supported target. The game validates contents, remaining uses and target prerequisites before applying effects.

knowledgeDescription: The protagonist initially knows their friend and the square. Other records may be inspected by the author, including those unknown to the protagonist. Knowledge is independent of visibility.
